records.note: Cdk1-dependent DIAPH1 phosphorylation maintained suitable cortical tension; phosphorylation mutants increased tension and delayed anaphase. This is mitotic-cortex mechanics, not muscle force.
records.uncertainty: This model and endpoint do not establish an administered treatment benefit for skeletal-muscle function or BUB1B-related disease; genetic/mechanistic results are not transferred to drugs.

records.title: SARS-CoV-2 potential drugs, drug targets, and biomarkers: a viral-host interaction network-based analysis.

records.note: Network analysis nominated multiple cytotoxic/cardiac drugs and neem/HMOX1 strategies; no drugs were administered in the described study and no muscle benefit was measured.
records.uncertainty: Associative, diagnostic or computational evidence does not establish a therapeutic rescue; no direct skeletal-muscle or BUB1B treatment benefit is shown.

records.title: Anti-tumor target screening of sea cucumber saponin Frondoside A: a bioinformatics and molecular docking analysis.

administered_agents.name: Frondoside A
administered_agents.role: administered to liver, pancreatic and bladder cancer cell lines

records.note: Frondoside A reduced cancer-cell viability/migration; proposed pathway regulation includes muscle-contraction genes in bladder cancer, not demonstrated normal-muscle contractile benefit.

records.title: Mitotic DNA damage promotes chromokinesin-mediated missegregation of polar chromosomes in cancer cells.

administered_agents.name: etoposide
administered_agents.role: explicitly named topoisomerase-II inhibitor inducing mitotic DNA damage

records.model: Mitotic cancer cells and pan-cancer colony assays
records.note: Chemotherapy-induced mitotic DNA damage caused misaligned/polar chromosome missegregation and micronuclei with variable cytotoxicity; etoposide was explicitly named.
records.uncertainty: The stated effect includes induced missegregation/micronuclei, not genomic repair. No normal-muscle/tissue-preservation benefit was shown.

records.title: An ATM/Chk2-mediated DNA damage-responsive signaling pathway suppresses Epstein-Barr virus transformation of primary human B cells.

administered_agents.name: ATM/Chk2 inhibition
administered_agents.role: Intervention reported; pharmacological versus genetic modality and agent identities not specified

records.note: EBV-associated early hyperproliferation activated a growth-suppressive DNA-damage response; ATM/Chk2 inhibition increased transformation efficiency and EBNA3C attenuated the response.

records.title: The Human-Specific and Smooth Muscle Cell-Enriched LncRNA SMILR Promotes Proliferation by Regulating Mitotic CENPF mRNA and Drives Cell-Cycle Progression Which Can Be Targeted to Limit Vascular Remodeling.

administered_agents.name: SMILR siRNA
administered_agents.role: RNA knockdown administered in cultured cells and ex vivo vein graft

records.model: Human vascular SMCs and ex vivo saphenous-vein grafts
records.note: SMILR siRNA reduced ex vivo proliferation from about 29% to 5%; knockdown also increased binucleated cells by about 10%, linking benefit to altered cytokinesis.
records.uncertainty: The antiproliferative benefit is specific to vascular-remodeling models and accompanies increased binucleation. RNA administration is not equivalent to an approved medicine; no skeletal-muscle function or MVA rescue is shown.

records.title: A common molecular mechanism underlies the role of Mps1 in chromosome biorientation and the spindle assembly checkpoint.
records.model: Yeast mps1-3 mutant
records.note: Suppressors lowering PP1 at Spc105 or forced Bub1-Spc105 association restored both chromosome biorientation and SAC signaling in mps1-3 cells. Rescue was genetic and lesion-specific.
records.uncertainty: The rescued lesion is mps1-3 in yeast and the interventions are genetic. It supplies a checkpoint-scaffold mechanism, not an administered drug or BUB1B-specific benefit.

records.title: An Eighteen-Gene Classifier Predicts Locoregional Recurrence in Post-Mastectomy Breast Cancer Patients.
records.model: Independent cohort of 135 post-mastectomy breast-cancer patients without PMRT
